name: Fail-first red-proof certification as an external gate
description: Certify, from OUTSIDE the author's own discipline, that a change's own test was RED before the fix - so a test that could never fail cannot be presented as a regression test. Mechanical and fully deterministic given the refs: check out the pre-change ref, run the NAMED tests (they must fail), run them post-change (they must pass), and STORE the runner's real output as the capture rather than asserting it. A test that passes at the pre-change ref is not a regression proof for this change. An unbuildable pre-change tree makes the certification UNAVAILABLE - never assumed.

diff_path.description: The change whose test claim is being certified

test_ids.description: The tests the change CLAIMS as its proof; each is certified or refused individually

pre_change_ref.description: The ref the tests must FAIL at

post_change_ref.description: The ref the tests must PASS at

pure_addition_allowed.description: A new-feature test with no prior behaviour has nothing to be red about; substitute a mutation check instead of forcing a fake red

evidence_store.description: Where the runner's real stdout is stored per certified test

certifier.description: Runs the named tests at both refs and stores the real runner output

addition-adjudicator.description: Decides whether a test is a pure addition and routes it to the mutation substitute

routes.reason: the pure-addition escape is the one place this gate can be talked out of firing

stages.title: Which tests does the change claim as its proof?

work_unit.title: Identify the tests a change claims as its proof and split pure additions from regression tests
work_unit.question_or_target: Resolve each claimed test id to a real test, and classify it: a REGRESSION test asserts behaviour that existed and broke, so it must be red at the pre-change ref; a PURE ADDITION covers behaviour that did not exist, so there is nothing to be red about and forcing a fake red would be fabrication. Say which is which and why.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: misclassifying a regression test as a pure addition is how this gate gets bypassed

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each test id resolves to a real node id, and its classification cites the pre-change source that either did or did not contain the behaviour
tests_required: a test asserting behaviour present before the change must classify REGRESSION, not PURE-ADDITION
both-states control: a test for a brand-new function must classify PURE-ADDITION and route to the mutation substitute
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the red-before gate is mechanical; the classification is the only judgement and it is recorded
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:QLT-5901 emitted only when every claimed test id resolves and carries a REGRESSION or PURE-ADDITION classification with its justification; otherwise FAILED:QLT-5901 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to classifying REGRESSION (the stricter path) and say so

stages.title: At the pre-change ref the named tests must FAIL
An unbuildable pre-change tree makes this UNAVAILABLE, not assumed
A test that passes pre-change is not a regression proof
At the post-change ref the named tests must PASS
A test still failing after the change certifies nothing
The red capture must be the runner's real output, stored
For a pure addition, substitute mutation evidence of protective power
Per test: CERTIFIED, REFUSED, or UNAVAILABLE

work_unit.title: Emit a per-test certification with the stored red and green captures
work_unit.question_or_target: For each claimed test emit CERTIFIED (red at pre, green at post, both captures stored), REFUSED (passed at pre, so it proves nothing about this change), SUBSTITUTED (pure addition, mutation evidence attached) or UNAVAILABLE (pre-change tree would not build). No aggregate verdict may be more favourable than its worst per-test outcome.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the certification is the deliverable and is fully determined by the stored captures

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the stored runner stdout for both refs, per test, with the exact node id and both git refs recorded
tests_required: a test that passes before the change must be REFUSED as a proof, not certified
both-states control: a genuine regression test must CERTIFY, so the gate is not a blanket refusal
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none required - the captures are the evidence and a reviewer cannot overturn them
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:QLT-5902 emitted only when every claimed test has one of the four verdicts with its stored captures, and the aggregate is no better than the worst per-test outcome; otherwise FAILED:QLT-5902 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to emitting UNAVAILABLE with the build error attached
work_unit.mechanism: two-ref outcome pairing over author-named tests with stored captures
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: the spec-blind synthesis blueprint also runs two trees, but its tests are synthesised behind an information barrier; here the tests are the AUTHOR'S OWN and the question is whether they were ever red

impact.blast_radius: checks out a pre-change ref in a separate worktree and runs named tests; writes captures under command-center/test/**

x_extensions.mechanism: Replay the author's OWN named tests at two git refs and require the red-then-green pattern, storing the runner output as the capture. No generation, no mutation, no reading - just two executions and a stored artifact.
contraindications: NOT for tests added alongside brand-new behaviour - there is nothing to be red about, so a mutation substitute is used instead of a fake red
NOT usable when the pre-change tree will not build - the verdict is UNAVAILABLE, never assumed
NOT a judgement of test QUALITY, only of whether the test could ever have failed

benchmark_cases.name: passes-before-change
benchmark_cases.setup: a test that is green at the pre-change ref
benchmark_cases.expected: REFUSED as a proof for this change

benchmark_cases.name: genuine-regression-test
benchmark_cases.setup: a test that fails pre-change and passes post-change

x_extensions.why_not_a_duplicate: BP-IMP-04 is the implementation LOOP that produces a red proof; this is the external CERTIFIER of one, usable on work you did not write. BP-TST-03 shares the two-execution harness but its tests are synthesised behind an information barrier and it returns SPEC-MISS, a verdict this blueprint cannot produce.
x_extensions.unverified: UNVERIFIED (very-likely) how many past 'fixed with a test' commits carry no red proof; settling experiment = certify the last 20 such commits and count. The MECHANISM is almost-certain (fully deterministic given the refs); only the yield is unmeasured.

worked_example.name: certify the two tests a predicate bug-fix commit claims as its proof
worked_example.narrative: Both tests classified REGRESSION. At HEAD~1 both failed and the runner stdout was stored verbatim; at HEAD both passed. Both CERTIFIED. No pure additions, so the mutation substitute did not run.

negative_control.why: a test that was already green cannot be a regression proof for this change; this is the single most common way a green suite lies
